takeaway: Another sunny, breezy, hot day. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds this morning on the North Pacific, a chance of scattered showers on the peninsula this afternoon, and Nicoya near 34°C. The trade winds pick up a notch today as the season's first cold push brushes the region, with gusts of 30–45 km/h possible in Guanacaste. For surf, it's offshore today and every day through at least Monday, with a 17-second south-southwest swell at 5–7 feet today, easing over the weekend. The rest of October looks mostly dry. The one new wrinkle is that the models now bring a wetter spell close to Nosara around Nov 3–5, which goes against IMN's dry outlook. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Thu–Sat, Oct 22–24)
periods.pattern: IMN's Thursday forecast for the North Pacific is few clouds and moderate wind in the morning, then partly cloudy with possible scattered showers on the peninsula in the afternoon. Tonight is partly cloudy with wind in the mountains. Nicoya's high is about 34°C (Liberia near 37°C) and the low about 23°C. IMN says the stronger trade winds are pulling clouds and rain to the Caribbean side and the Northern Zone, not to us. The model averages show light rain near Nosara: roughly 5–10 mm (a quarter to a third of an inch) per day today through Saturday, with Friday the wettest in the European averages. The marine forecast also mentions scattered showers and a few storms offshore tonight and Friday night.
periods.implications: Good outdoor days with sun, heat, and a steady breeze. A passing afternoon or overnight shower is possible but should be brief. Mornings are the coolest and calmest time for anything active.
periods.confidence: High on breezy, mostly sunny days. Moderate on whether a brief shower clips Nosara on Friday.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sun–Wed, Oct 25–28)
periods.pattern: All the model averages keep a steady northeast-to-east breeze across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica, and the marine forecast has the winds strengthening Monday, with 20–25 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo. Rain near Nosara drops to only a few millimeters a day, with the heaviest rain staying on the Caribbean side and offshore to the south. IMN's weekly outlook still has the cold push bringing drier air and occasional moderate winds to the North Pacific this weekend.
periods.implications: Probably the driest, breeziest stretch so far this season. Expect sunny beach days and lower humidity, with a stiff breeze at times, especially Monday.
periods.confidence: High on breezy and mostly dry.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Thu Oct 29 – Thu Nov 5)
periods.pattern: The trades keep blowing over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica into early November in every model. Through about Nov 1 it stays mostly dry near Nosara. After that, all three model averages bring the band of tropical showers that sits south of Costa Rica back north toward the Nicoya coast. The American average shows close to an inch a day near Nosara on Nov 3–4, the European average gets there by Nov 4–5, and the AI-based European average is lighter at about 10 mm a day. IMN's updated long-range outlook (now Oct 26–Nov 22) disagrees. It calls for drier-than-normal weather across the country, extra-dry conditions on the North Pacific through Nov 1, and the dry season taking hold on the North and Central Pacific during the first week of November.
periods.implications: The end of October looks good for outdoor plans. Keep plans for Nov 3–5 flexible, because the models and IMN don't agree yet.
periods.confidence: Moderate-high on a dry end to October. Low on early November.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades, offshore at Nosara, every day from today through at least Monday. It's a firm, steady offshore pattern, and it strengthens again Sunday and Monday.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 2:05 a.m. PDT Thursday, 3:05 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds at 15–20 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo today and northeast 10–15 knots elsewhere, which is offshore here. Tonight it's north to northeast 10–15. Friday and Saturday it's northeast 10–15 by day and about 10 at night. Sunday is northeast to east 15–20 in the gulf and about 10 elsewhere, and Monday is northeast 20–25 in the gulf and 10–15 elsewhere. One caution: the waters just south of the peninsula have light, variable winds that turn southwest around 10 knots Friday afternoon. Nosara sits near that edge, so on lighter afternoons a sea breeze can still add texture. Swell: south to southwest 5–7 feet at 17 seconds today, 4–6 feet at 16 seconds tonight, 4–6 feet at 15 seconds Friday, 4–6 feet at 14 seconds Saturday, 3–5 feet at 13 seconds Sunday, then a west swell around 4–6 feet at 12 seconds Sunday night and 3–5 feet Monday. Nicaragua: every model keeps solid easterly trades over Nicaragua for the full two weeks, so Nicaragua should be offshore all day most days. That's a strong sign of good wind for Nosara mornings, but it doesn't mean Nosara is offshore all day every day.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today: the best morning of the run, with firm offshore wind and the 17-second swell at 5–7 feet. Get out early. Friday and Saturday mornings: clean and offshore, with a slightly smaller, shorter-period swell. Sunday and Monday mornings: offshore and windier, but the swell is down to about 3–5 feet. Long-period sets will be bigger and farther apart than the average height suggests, so choose your spot carefully.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore through Monday from the marine forecast. High on the swell trend. Moderate on how late into each afternoon the offshore holds.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, low. Nothing established and nothing building in the next 10 days.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: The only signal is a wetter spell around Nov 3–5 in the model averages. That's at the far end of the forecast.
gyreWatch.supporting: All three model averages bring the shower band south of Costa Rica back north toward Nicoya in early November, with near-Nosara amounts close to an inch a day on Nov 3–4 in the American average and Nov 4–5 in the European average.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model shows a broad, slow-spinning low near Costa Rica, and all of them keep northeast-to-east trades over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica into early November. A prolonged soak needs days of steady wind from the Pacific, which is the opposite. IMN's long-range outlook calls for drier-than-normal weather through Nov 22 and sees no extreme events Oct 26–Nov 1. Tropical Storm Vance is far south-southwest of Acapulco and heading away. Nothing is expected near Central America in the Pacific or the Caribbean. The U.S. tropics outlook (updated Oct 20) says East Pacific storm activity should wind down entering November.

whatChanged: The marine forecast now keeps the offshore wind going through Monday, and Monday's gulf winds pick up to 20–25 knots. The swell is holding as forecast at 17 seconds today, with a new, shorter west swell showing up Sunday night. The system south of Mexico became Tropical Storm Vance and is moving away. IMN updated its long-range outlook, which now runs Oct 26–Nov 22 and calls for drier-than-normal weather across the country. It now says the dry season should take hold on the North and Central Pacific in the first week of November. The models went the other way at the far end. Yesterday they showed early-November rain creeping up to about 10 mm a day near Nosara, and today the American and European averages show close to an inch a day around Nov 3–5.
practical: Today: surf the morning in offshore wind and a 17-second swell, then expect a hot, breezy afternoon around 34°C with a small chance of a passing shower. Friday and Saturday: more good surf mornings and sunny beach days. Sunday to Wednesday: dry and windy, so it's a good time for outdoor plans, though the surf will be smaller. Keep Nov 3–5 plans flexible. Long-period swell means stronger currents, so watch for rips. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
